source.note: Supplied offline evidence; URL not verified by importer. Specs from Slack.fr's own shop page as captured 2014-08-29; product_url is that Wayback capture, because shop.slack.fr is long gone (Slack.fr's catalogue is now carried by Slack Inov) - hence active false. The capture confirms, unchanged, the four figures this row already held from the SlackDB import: flat, 100 % polyester, 25 mm, 62 g/m, MBS 28 kN. Two things it adds. (1) Elongation: the maker states 5.5 % at 15 kN, recorded as a second stretch point beside the inherited 4.7 % at 10 kN - two single quoted figures, not a measured curve. (2) Price: the shop sells three lengths, 25 m at 49 EUR, 50 m at 79 EUR and 100 m at 145 EUR, i.e. 1.96, 1.58 and 1.45 EUR/m. priceMeter was 1.96, which is exactly the 25 m tier - the dearest per metre of the three. It is set here to 1.45, the 100 m line this capture is the page for, matching the 2FACES entry's rule of taking the longest length's regular price; the ladder is recorded above so the other tiers are not lost. Prices include the made-up line, not bulk webbing by the metre. The maker calls the product Superflat "Dark Blue"; the catalogue name stays "Dark Blue" because the id and name are already recorded elsewhere. Polyester at 28 kN derives Type B.

source.note: Supplied offline evidence; URL not verified by importer. Specs confirmed direct by Wall Ace (2026-09-10), superseding the announcement-post figures this entry was first built from: 25 mm, 36 g/m (not 27.5), MBS 27 kN. That MBS is the strength of the webbing terminated in loops - the way the product is actually sold and used - not a raw tensile figure for the band, and it is what the derived classification is computed from. Construction is a Dyneema centre with purple nylon edges. Production has stopped - the maker's own summary of this webbing and its thinner twin, Duct Tape, is "comfortable and cheap but not exactly high tech" - so active is false, and there is no product page (product_url null). The announcement post this entry was first built from, which had a first length reaching Australia and a main shipment a month out, described the end of the run rather than the start of one. Sizing: sold only as a complete highline kit, and always in the same two segments - a 75 m main and an 83 m backup (4 loops included), at an indicative, not-yet-finalised ~580 AUD for the kit. No priceMeter is recorded: `price` on a webbing is per metre, and dividing an unfinalised kit price by 158 m would invent a number the maker has not quoted. Stretch is recorded as null, deliberately. The maker's own account is that it is very hard to put one figure on: roughly 5% between 1 and 3 kN, then about 2.5% more between 3 and 5 kN - so on the order of 7.5% total at 5 kN - with the curve flattening off as load climbs further. That is a shape described from memory, not a measured curve, and the earlier single 2.5% at 5 kN point taken from the announcement post was wrong by a factor of three. A wrong curve on a chart is worse than no curve. Photos: the two Wall Ace webbing images we hold are shared between Steel Cable and Duct Tape. The products are the same weave in two thicknesses, and the maker's own view is that the same picture serves both - and that the one filed under Steel Cable may in fact be Duct Tape. Which image is which is not settled.
